The retrieved FY2025 Item 1A text from JPMorganChase does not use the words "absolute security." It does say it "cannot guarantee that it will always detect cybersecurity threats" or "implement effective preventive measures." Among the reasons it lists, attack techniques evolve frequently and grow more sophisticated, so an attack may go unrecognized until launched or undetected for long periods. It also does not control the cybersecurity of its many clients, customers, counterparties and third-party service providers. Separately, the filing says the firm could become more vulnerable if it does not identify and address emerging threats, known vulnerabilities or control shortcomings in a timely way. That point comes from a different passage and is not one of the listed reasons.
JPMorganChase states in its FY2025 10-K risk factors that it "cannot guarantee that it will always detect cybersecurity threats to its systems or implement effective preventive measures against those threats." This is the closest language to the question's premise. The exact phrase "absolute security" was not found in the retrieved Item 1A text.
One reason JPMorganChase gives is that the techniques used in cyber attacks evolve frequently and increase in sophistication. As a result, an attack may not be recognized until it is launched or may go undetected for extended periods.
Another reason JPMorganChase gives is that it does not control the cybersecurity of the systems of the numerous clients, customers, counterparties and third-party service providers with which it does business. Elsewhere it adds that its cybersecurity risks could also affect its vendors or other interconnected third parties.
In a separate passage, JPMorganChase says it could become increasingly vulnerable to cyber attacks if it does not identify and address emerging threats, known vulnerabilities or shortcomings in its cybersecurity controls in a timely manner. It cites zero-day vulnerabilities, meaning unknown security flaws in software and hardware, as an example. It also notes that a transition to quantum-resistant encryption may not be completed before relevant threats become operational.
JPMorganChase says it experiences numerous cyber attacks on its computer systems, software, networks and other technology assets.
question: Why does JPMorgan Chase say it cannot guarantee absolute security against cyberattacks?
